facts.text: Portage earned its name from the short, two‑mile portage between the Fox and Wisconsin Rivers that early explorers used to reach the Mississippi.
The city’s slogan, "Where the North Begins," reflects its historic role as a gateway between the Midwest and the northern frontier.
Fort Winnebago’s Surgeon’s Quarters, now a museum, stands on the site where the federal government first built a post in 1828 to protect the portage trade.
Portage’s downtown streets once housed a bustling commercial hub that served traders from Green Bay to Prairie du Chien during the 19th‑century fur‑trade boom.
The city’s historic district includes the Zona Gale House, honoring the Pulitzer‑winning author who grew up in Portage and wrote about life in the Midwest.
Amtrak’s Empire Builder stops in Portage, connecting the city to Chicago and the Pacific Northwest along a route that echoes the old Fox‑Wisconsin waterway.
